sources.title: Margaret Jacobs, review of Sarah Carter, Imperial Plots
sources.citation: Margaret Jacobs, review of Imperial Plots, Manitoba History84(Summer2017), original publisher online text.

verification.note: Read original publisher main assessment and complete concluding objections in the two retained browser witnesses. Jacobs praises the complex gender/colonial argument but asks about the scale and influence of British/Canadian women’s organizations and the unresolved comparative paradox of Canada’s more restrictive homestead gender policy. Publication2017 is distinct from page revision2020. Jacobs lacks a full endpoint; neither her historical claims nor Carter’s whole book are independently verified.

screq_carter_2008.note: Additional selected primary reading from the actual AU Press open publisher PDF: opening passages3–6 and8–17, selected acknowledgmentsxi–xii,31,64–67 and277, plus their exact notes and bibliography. Cott, Perry, Van Kirk, Stoler, Brown, Thompson and Burton retain distinct work-specific roles. Chapter7 note150 concerns Burton’s edited collection and authored introduction. Stoler locators are31 and64, not16. Thompson’s customary-divorce argument retains the property qualification; Brown’s warning preserves varied unions and scarce Indigenous wives’ testimony. Earlier3–9reading remains intact. No whole399-page PDF/book or cited original work reading, legal validation or universal Indigenous marriage model is claimed.

p4b_carter_2016.note: Additional selected3–9 passages and corresponding notes/bibliography read in the actual Manitoba publisher PDF, corrected2018reprint of2016book. Earlier selected3–11/19–23 record is preserved, not silently extended to wholebook reading. Explicit Wolfe formulation6/note6, Levine and shared Tosh framing7–8/notes13,20, and Perry liberal-order quotations8/notes22–23 have specified argumentative uses. Settler women’s exclusion and participation in dispossession remain jointly qualified; historical quotes are objects of Carter’s analysis, not the atlas’s voice. General acknowledgment and editorial roles do not automatically establish formation. Original cited works remain unread.

df01_ahenakew_medicine2003.note: Reread the complete signed Medicine review196–197 in publisher PDF leaves2–3, beginning after the preceding Alfred Fisher review. Harold Cardinal, Paul Chartrand, Ahenakew and Dickason are Medicine-attributed scholarly resources. Her quoted Christine Welsh discussion and Big Bear example are distinct; no relay of those claims to Ahenakew or Dickason. Existing edges1701/1715 remain, with Carter’s1999survey and underlying originals unread.

df02_dickason_carter2001_review.note: Retained original repository review text confirms Dickason’s corrective-history praise and idealization/equality criticism already represented by edge1712. No fresh facsimile or1999book reading is claimed; the original review page235 and sole reviewer remain distinct from the repository’s metadata. Her reception and Medicine’s reported Dickason resource coexist.
